intro.en: More of the body, and what to say when you fall, cut yourself or burn yourself.

torcerse.nota: O becomes ue: me torcí el tobillo.

texto.en:
Accidents to your own body use a verb in **-se** and the article: **me he roto el** brazo; **me he cortado el** dedo; **me quemé la** mano; **me torcí el** tobillo; **me di un golpe en la** cabeza.

**Caerse** is to fall: **me caí** por la escalera; **se cayó** de la bici.

The story has a scene and an event: **estaba cocinando** y **me quemé**; **iba** en bici y **me caí**.

The results: **una herida**, **un corte**, **una quemadura**, **un golpe**.

The remedies: **una tirita**, **una venda**, **una escayola**, **hielo**. They **te ponen** una escayola and **te dan** puntos.

To ask: **¿Qué te ha pasado?** **¿Te has hecho daño?** **¿Te duele?**

frases.es: ¿Qué te ha pasado en el brazo?
Me lo he roto. Iba en bici, me caí y me di un golpe en el codo.
frases.en: I've broken it. I was on my bike, I fell and I banged my elbow.
How painful! Did they put a cast on?

frases.es: Sí, para un mes. Y me torcí el tobillo.
frases.en: Yes, for a month. And I sprained my ankle.

frases.es: Pues yo ayer me corté un dedo cocinando.
frases.en: Well, yesterday I cut my finger cooking.

frases.es: Menos mal que solo necesitas una tirita.
frases.en: Just as well you only need a plaster.

la.en: With me, Spanish uses the article.

mi.en: Me already says whose leg it is.

una.en: One of your own legs still takes la.

pregunta.en: Complete: I fell down the stairs.
What do you put on a small cut?

una escayola.en: That is for a broken bone.

pregunta.en: Complete: I was cooking and I burnt myself.

quemé.en: The accident is the event: indefinido.

quemaba.en: The imperfect would make it a background.

explicacion.en: Tobillo is the ankle and torcerse is to sprain.

bloques.frase: Me di un golpe en la cabeza

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about an accident, yours or someone else's: what happened and what the consequences were.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Explain aloud to a doctor how you hurt yourself.
